Commentary.Commentary: The umpires and the players have made their way out to the middle. Its Litton Das and Tanzid Hasan to open the batting for Bangladesh, chasing 230 in 50 overs. Aryan Dutt to start the attack for the Netherlands. Lets Play!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, Netherlands have posted a fighting total on the board but will need to be at their absolute best to defend it and if dew comes in, it will be even more difficult. Bangladesh will be confident about gunning this total down and getting their second win of the tournament. Join us in a bit to see how the chase unfolds.

Taskin Ahmed in his interview after the first innings, says that he missed the last two games due to a shoulder injury. Adds that it is an old injury which has flared up suddenly and there was tear so he did not bowl fit the last week or so but is feeling better now. Tells that they picked up wickets in the Powerplay after a few matches and this will give them confidence going forward in the tournament. Says the wicket is on the slower side but still good to bat on and hopes that they will be able to chase this down.

Bangladesh's bowlers showcased their prowess in this encounter, leaving their mark on the game. The likes of Mustafizur Rahman, Taskin Ahmed, and the skipper Shakib Al Hasan demonstrated their mettle. They meticulously deployed well-crafted deliveries during the middle overs, building pressure and reaping the rewards with the regular fall of wickets. Mustafizur and Taskin, each, claimed two wickets within their spells, while Shakib joined the wicket-taking procession with one scalping. Bangladesh's bowlers executed their plans masterfully, putting the Dutch batters under duress. However, it was with the fielding that Bangladesh displayed a few chinks in their armor. A couple of crucial catches off the blade of Scott Edwards in the 16th over eluded their grasp, allowing him to anchor the innings and steer the Netherlands to a respectable total. A chance at point was also missed of Sybrand Engelbrecht, denying them another breakthrough. While the fielding was generally decent, these lapses serve as reminders of the fine margins that can shape the destiny of a cricket match. Bangladesh, well aware of the need to clinch a victory tonight to ascend the points table, will take these developments in stride as they prepare for their chase. Facing a target of 230 on a wicket that plays true and offers assistance under the evening lights, the task at hand shouldn't be overly daunting if they can maintain a steady flow of wickets early in their innings.

The Netherlands' journey at the crease was a blend of resilience and some early setbacks. In the opening phase, they lost two wickets, falling prey to the skilled Bangladeshi pacers within the initial 10 overs. Yet, from the ashes of adversity, resilience emerged. Wesley Barresi, one of the Dutch warriors, alongside Colin Ackermann, embarked on a mission to salvage their innings. The pair stitched together a 59-run partnership, taking the fight to the Bangladeshi camp. However, Barresi's brave stand came to an end when he amassed 41 runs from 41 deliveries. Soon after, Ackermann, too, departed to the mighty Shakib Al Hasan, and Scott Edwards, the Dutch skipper, shouldered the responsibility of rebuilding the innings. His innings was a masterpiece in itself, a brilliant half-century carved meticulously, encompassing 68 runs from 89 balls. Edwards formed vital alliances with Bas de Leede and Sybrand Engelbrecht, ensuring the Netherlands batted into the 45th over. However, his splendid run came to a halt when a slower delivery from Mustafizur Rahman outside the off-stump got the better of him. After Edwards' departure, the Bangladeshi bowlers exhibited immaculate control, stifling the Dutch, who managed to amass 229 runs by the end of their innings, setting a target of 230 for Bangladesh as they prepare to embark on their chase.

As the sun dips below the horizon and the enchanting evening atmosphere envelops the Eden Gardens in Kolkata, the first innings of Match No. 28 in the ICC Men's World Cup 2023 comes to a close. In this contest, it's Bangladesh pitted against the Netherlands, and the coin had its say with the Dutch skipper opting to set a target by batting first. On a pitch that appears tailor-made for the art of batting, the Netherlands battled valiantly and put up a total of 229 for the loss of all their wickets in their quota of 50 overs.

PITCH REPORT - Samuel Badree says that from the clubhouse end it is 76 meters on the long on region and a short pocket on the third man. Ramiz Raja joins him and says it is a solid batting pitch. Adds that there's hardly any blade of grass at the full-length or good-length area which will disturb batters, and conditions are ripe for big striking. Tells there might be a little bit of spin but we can expect a high-scoring game.

Shakib Al Hasan, the captain of Bangladesh says that they have to be better with both bat and ball in the Powerplay. Adds that he is fine with bowling first here and it is always good to play in Kolkata. He expects the support to be great as well. Informs they have also made two changes as Taskin Ahmed and Mahedi Hasan replaces Hasan Mahmud and Nasum Ahmed respectively.

Scott Edwards, the skipper of Netherlands says that they will bat first. Adds that the wicket looks good and they want to get off to a quick start as well. Tells that they have set high expectations for themselves and they need to perform to their potential here. Informs they have made a couple of changes as Wesley Barresi and Shariz Ahmad come in for this match.

Netherlands (Playing XI) - Vikramjit Singh, Max O'Dowd, Wesley Barresi (In place of Teja Nidamanuru), Colin Ackermann, Scott Edwards (C/WK), Bas de Leede, Sybrand Engelbrecht, Logan van Beek, Shariz Ahmad (In place of Roelof van der Merwe), Aryan Dutt, Paul van Meekeren.
TOSS - Netherlands have won the toss and they have elected to BAT first.

Conversely, Bangladesh began their World Cup journey on a positive note with an initial win, but they have subsequently suffered four consecutive losses. Their chances of securing a spot in the top four teams of the tournament now appear slim. In their recent encounter against South Africa, they too suffered a heavy loss. Their bowling needs to improve massively while their middle order also start performing. Shakib Al Hasan will be once again the key player for them but Mahmudullah has been in exceptional form and also scored a hundred against the Proteas and will be important too. They now faces the task of regrouping, refining their strategies, and aim for the two points as they know they can't slip up anymore.

The Netherlands' recent performance was a bitter pill to swallow, as they faced the mighty Australian team. The Dutch bowlers found it challenging to contain the Aussies but will be confident about putting up a challenge in this game. Among the bowlers, Logan van Beek was a standout performer, claiming four wickets for 74 runs. Unfortunately, their batters too crumbled under the pressure of the massive target and were dismissed for a mere 90 runs.
